questions.sub_skill: Manage permissions and roles in Security Copilot
questions.prompt: Your organisation onboards Security Copilot. A finance user discovers they can open the portal. Why?
options: Their Entra role inherits Copilot owner
Copilot contributor is granted to every user in the Microsoft Entra tenant by default; restricting it is a deliberate act
Security Copilot is licensed per tenant, so all users are entitled
The workspace was created without role assignments
questions.explanation: Onboarding opens the platform to the directory rather than to the SOC. Note what restricting it does and does not change: it governs who can use the platform, not what they can see once inside.

questions.prompt: An analyst holding Compliance Administrator reports that Copilot answers Microsoft Purview questions well but returns nothing for Sentinel. Explain.
options: The Sentinel plugin is in preview and unavailable to non-owners
Copilot inherits the signed-in user's existing permissions; their Purview role grants Purview data access, and reaching Sentinel data needs its own role assignment
Plugins can only be enabled one at a time per workspace
Sentinel data requires a separate SCU allocation
questions.explanation: A Copilot role grants no access to underlying security data. Two analysts running the same prompt legitimately get different answers, and an empty result means no data or no access — a permissions question, not a prompt question.

questions.prompt: Provisioning capacity fails for an administrator who holds Global Administrator in the tenant. Most likely cause?
options: Global Administrator cannot provision capacity; only Security Administrator can
They lack Azure Contributor or Owner on the subscription or resource group — capacity is an Azure resource, and both permissions are required
The tenant has no Security Copilot licence assigned to that user
Capacity must be provisioned from the Azure portal, not the Copilot portal
questions.explanation: Provisioning needs Azure Contributor or Owner on the subscription or resource group, plus Security Administrator or higher in the tenant. Neither alone is sufficient, and discovering that after a failed attempt wastes session time you are paying for.

questions.sub_skill: Enable and configure Microsoft agents and Security Store agents
questions.prompt: Your SCU bill has tripled and analyst usage is unchanged. What do you check first?
options: The number of plugins enabled per workspace
Scheduled agents, which consume capacity continuously whether or not anyone reads their output
The workspace's geo, which affects unit pricing
Whether custom plugins are calling external APIs
questions.explanation: Agents run defined security work on a schedule and draw from the capacity of the workspace they are assigned to. An agent enabled and forgotten is a recurring charge with nobody watching the output — check agents before people.

questions.prompt: Different teams need different capacity budgets, different plugin sets, and data stored in different regions for compliance. What is the unit of segmentation?
options: One tenant per team, linked by Azure Lighthouse
Workspaces — each holds its own capacity, plugin configuration, role assignments and data storage geo, chosen at creation
Plugin scopes, applied per user group
Separate SCU allocations against a single workspace
questions.explanation: A workspace is the unit of segmentation, and the geo selection is a data residency decision made at creation rather than a performance setting. Capacity can be moved between workspaces afterwards; the geo cannot.
